text:
incident-bot: autopager fired -> host gpu-rack-117-host-22 (node gpu-node-22)
  reason: kubelet NotReady + lost heartbeat + GPU not responding
  alert_id: PD-67321

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert PD-67321 created and sent to on-call

maria: acked PD-67321 :white_check_mark:
  I'll take first responder.

aj: oncall acked? paging me as secondary if not resolved in 10m.

maria: yep i have it. first check: ping & kubectl
  running: `kubectl get nodes gpu-node-22 -o wide` -> STATUS Unknown, KERNEL: ?

kube-bot: kubectl result pasted:
```
NAME          STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-22   Unknown  gpu      42d   v1.27.3
```

maria: trying `ssh root@gpu-rack-117-host-22` -> ssh timing out intermittently, connecting now

ryan: fyi saw a flurry of evictions for pods with gpu requests about ~08:12 UTC, might be related

maria: attached serial console over IPMI, grabbing logs:
```
[  +0.000000] kernel: NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:3b:00:00: GPU appears stuck, reset failed
[  +0.003456] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: GPU reset failure
[  +0.010000] watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 22s
```

aj: kernel panic on GPU reset. escalate to SRE lead. setting severity P1->P0? need impact first.

maria: customer impact check: routing shows spike in 503s to model endpoints that were scheduled on that node's tenant pool between 08:10-08:15 UTC. Preliminary: ~0.8% of hosted requests, 3 dedicated jobs dropped and restarted. Not platform-wide.

sophia: posting to incidents channel for visibility and asking trust/sales for any enterprise customers pinned to that rack.

maria: mitigation actions I'm running now:
  - cordon node: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-22`
  - drain best-effort: `kubectl drain gpu-node-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
  - create temp routing fallback for model assignments from that rack

maria: drain output started, a couple pods stuck (nvidia-device-plugin daemonset ok, but one stateful model-server refuses termination)

aj: i'll try graceful restart of kubelet via IPMI script, but kernel panic suggests host-level RMA. please keep draining so workload moves off.

ryan: adding eviction tolerance to scheduler for models in progress to reduce tail errors while we shift capacity. pushing config change to autoscaler to spin up extra dedicated capacity in us-west-2 to absorb churn.

maria: record of commands & outputs saved to S3: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/3890012345/logs.txt

sre-bot: Escalation note: vendor ticket opened with GPU vendor, severity HIGH, RMA initiated for host 117-22. Ticket ref VEND-9012. ETA site tech 6-8 hours.

aj: since ETA long, plan B: continue replacement with spare capacity, and for any enterprise pinned workloads we will offer failover to Dedicated pool and a credit. @sophia handle comms once we confirm list.

maria: post-mortem notes in progress. immediate timeline:
  - 08:10 UTC: autopager fired
  - 08:11 UTC: on-call ack (maria)
  - 08:13 UTC: ssh/serial access, kernel panic logs collected
  - 08:15 UTC: cordon & drain started
  - 08:18 UTC: autoscaler requested extra capacity, started provisioning
  - 08:22 UTC: majority of GPU workloads rescheduled to other nodes, error spike subsided

sophia: I pinged account team for two customers that had model shards on that rack; they're aware, will coordinate comms if they request postmortem.

maria: moving to handoff to Aj for long-running RMA and vendor coordination. leaving notes in runbook: "gpu-host-kernel-panic".

aj: taking over. if anything else pops, ping me and I'll wake vendor contact. I'll also check if we should ban a particular BIOS/driver combo from auto-deploy.

maria: thanks all — i'll update thread with final list of affected tenant ids and postmortem link when ready.

pagerduty: PD-67321 acknowledged by maria; status: acknowledged -> in progress

incident-bot: follow-up scheduled in 3h for postmortem draft reminder

sophia: marking follow-ups: ops-runbook update, autoscaler policy tweak, customer comms template.

maria: closing immediate response. last check: node remains unreachable for kubelet, workloads stable on fallback. handing to aj.

aj: confirmed takeover. setting incident status -> monitoring -> remediation in progress.
